verdict.tagline: A legendary survival horror milestone despite notoriously clunky controls.
for_you_if: you want to experience a foundational horror classic
you appreciate iconic action design and heavy atmosphere
not_for_you_if: you need modern fluid aiming and movement
you are unwilling to install community performance fixes
you despise escort protection sections and companion management

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's controls and movement as outdated, janky, and difficult to get used to compared to modern standards.

citations.review_text: Playing this one (on Switch 2) after having played the Remake. The controls are a bit janky but it adds to the horror in a way you only see in a couple titles (Dead Space for instance). While the Remake has smoother gameplay for sure, this one's ambiance is way better, plus it has a lot of charm to it in places where the Remake is lacking. It's so interesting to see which parts of the game are different.

Great game even though its age definitely shows.
The gunplay can feel a bit funny at times and some mechanics are outdated compared to modern games but it's still a lot of fun.
I personally prefer the remake because of the improved graphics and gameplay which i care about a lot even tho they removed some good cutscenes but I love both versions and think theyre both nice and worth playing :D
Worst controls for a game ever.

Resident Evil 4 — A Legendary Game Held Back by Its Controls

I love the Resident Evil series for its story, characters, and overall lore, but honestly, playing the original Resident Evil 4 today feels very difficult. Just like Resident Evil 5, the controls are extremely outdated and uncomfortable. At times, it feels almost impossible to play smoothly by modern standards.

I understand why the game is considered legendary — it influenced an entire generation of action games and survival horror titles. The atmosphere, pacing, and iconic moments are still great. But the gameplay itself hasn’t aged well for me.

That’s why I really hope the remake handles things better. From what I’ve seen, the modernized controls and improved movement make the experience much more enjoyable while still preserving the spirit of the original.

I’ll always respect Resident Evil 4 for its impact on gaming, but personally, the original controls make it hard to fully enjoy today.

I love you daddy Leon. The controls are terrible though and I'd Highly recommend buying the remake. Game is quite difficult too but older games and all Resident Evils games are regardless, except maybe the more action focused 5 or 6.

From RE 0 to 4, worst RE I've played so far. The controls feel worse than any classic RE I've played, the voice acting is cringe (and very, very racist) and there's no horror / puzzle-solving experience at all. I'll have to give the remake a try.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the default tank controls and mouse movement as clunky or difficult to get used to when playing without mods.

citations.review_text:
From where I am in the game I believe I'm somewhere in the middle. Or at least mid-end. I genuinely do believe this is one of the greatest video games of all time and I know some people are complaining about this port, but there are mods to fix it. I don't remember the specific mod I installed but it literally fixed everything that people are complaining about in other reviews.

I can't say much about the Remake because I'm only early in that game, but this 2005 version of the game is absolutely worth your $20, especially if you mod it. The movement in this game was supposedly fixed by making everything directional controls instead of tank controls. This is a port of the older version of the game that had those tank controls that made the game more finnicky to play.

Compared to all of the other Resident Evil games, I would put this up there with some of the best stuff in the entire franchise. Yeah you're not fighting "real zombies" like in the other games, but there is a parasite spreading around the town that controls people as if they were zombies, and on top of that they speak Spanish. So if you understand that language you will get more out of this game than the average person.

Some of the worst parts about this game are Ashley. She is literally an escort mission for the entire game and I think that was a very bad decision. Some of the boss battles in this game can be somewhat buggy or at least somewhat hard to control, too. For being such a very good game that is one of the best in the franchise, those points feel much more minor than I'm actually making them out to be. For example if there's a bug going on with a boss, it usually fizzles out within a few minutes. Ashley can dodge stuff that comes her way so you won't get that many game overs because she got hit. Unless you're really sucking at the game, but that's a different matter altogether.

I forgot to talk about the level design which is some of the best in the entire series and probably the best in vi…

Yeah what they say is true. The most videogamey game to ever videogame. It took me a VERY long time to finish because the default tank controls are soooo bad if you're used to modern pc game WASD movement. I can't believe I actually made it like 75% through the game like that over a period of 5+ years.  Like I was having fun, but I would grow frustrated with the controls and drop the game for another year.

Once I installed the HD project with re4_tweaks mod is when it all finally clicked for me. I turned on the RE5 movement that makes Leon turn when I move the mouse left and right. I had a Danny Devito "I get it now" moment. I blasted through the remaining 25% and had the time of my life. 

I didn't grow up with this game so I feel like I'm not blinded by nostalgia as much as most people talking about it. So here's what I will say: It's really fun still. Shooting is some of the best in any game ever. 

However if you're more used to modern games I would recommend playing the remake first. The gameplay is much better and it trims a lot of the fat off this one. 

If you like the remake, then go ahead and play this one to appreciate the old school cheesy vibes.

I love the story and soundtracks, but the controls are really bad for me. I could play with the controller but my aim is trash so i use the mouse and keyboard instead, but it's not very convenient. 
Overall it's a fun game to play.

Resident Evil 4 has to be one of the best resident evil games out there. The first 40 minutes of gameplay will make you regret playing the games. It takes some time to get used to the tank aim controls even if you have played the first three original games. But once you get used to them ohhh boy is the game good. I cannot stop glazing this game. Its just sooo good. Highly recommended. 10/10.

Finally played it after all these years, there is almost no point no review a game like this since everyone already has a pre-established opinion on it, but ill give my feedback. 

The endless glaze of this game worried me that its going to be like half life 2, a boring game with infinitely shallow and repetitive combat. But no this is pretty fun, simple, yet fun to play. Now this isn't the greatest video game in the history of mankind far from it in fact RE4_tweaks is a must in order to play this game as it includes raw mouse support, fov options, vulkin renderer (that improves stability at high resolutions), allows your cpu to multitthread, toggle sprint, reload without having to aim and more fixes. This is awful to control when playing vanilla especially if you play M/K as the mouse is disorientating and clunky and its a chore to turn the character model. However the Ashley puzzle you need to disable this due to a freezing glitch, but other than that it works perfectly and make the game feel like a video game. Due to these improvements of mods the tank controls were perfectly fine, the gameplay itself is fun and satisfying even if there isn't much depth to it. Shoot, stun, kick, shoot, knee, suplex rhythm is fun to do, manage inventory and your money to figure out what you need, what to upgrade and what to sell and the game greatly rewards you for taking your time and exploring off the main path.

It's story overall is good and i can see why its considered a classic, though some of dialogue lacks any real emotion or depth especially at the scene where Leon and Ashley are removing the parasites, when its supposed to be a big moment. bosses here are mostly really good, except that damn lake monster, that has to be one of the most poorly programed bosses i have ever played in my life, its not its difficult its just wastes so much of your time. It wasn't until the end of chapter 4 where things go downhill, there is so much needless padding as the story drags its feet…

"An absolute classic that aged like fine wine."

The game that redefined the third-person shooter genre. Even in 2026, the pacing, enemy variety, and weapon upgrades are pure perfection. Tank controls take a few minutes to get used to, but once it clicks, it's non-stop fun.

Pros: Amazing pacing, satisfying gunplay, high replay value.
Cons: Classic tank controls aren't for everyone at first.

10/10 classic. Essential gaming history!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the laser sight dot disappears when aiming at targets that cannot be shot, which can cause the player to lose track of their aim.

citations.review_text:
Fantastic game, a huge change from the previous games, but still an absolute classic.

Graphics are excellent for the time, and even though they are definitely outdated by modern standards, they still hold up surprisingly well. The environments are varied and memorable, from the village and the castle to the island and underground facilities. Everything has its own atmosphere and identity, and the game does a great job of creating a constant feeling of danger. Character models are detailed for the time, and the enemy designs are fantastic, with the different Ganados and creatures being especially memorable. Some animations can feel a bit stiff today, but overall the presentation still looks great.

Sound effects are fantastic. The weapons sound powerful, the enemies make disturbing noises, and the environmental sounds do a great job of building tension. Hearing enemies shouting and communicating with each other makes encounters feel much more chaotic and dangerous. The soundtrack is also excellent, switching between tense atmospheric tracks, intense combat music, and quieter moments of exploration. The voice acting is much better than in the older games, although some of the dialogue and delivery can still be wonderfully cheesy. Some of the enemy Spanish voice lines are strangely hilarious.

Gameplay is great and very engaging. This is where Resident Evil 4 completely changed the formula. The camera moves behind Leon, allowing much more precise aiming and movement, and combat becomes a much bigger part of the experience. Unlike the previous games, you are expected to fight much more frequently, and the game gives you a huge variety of weapons to do it with. Handguns, shotguns, rifles, magnums, explosives, and other weapons all have their strengths and weaknesses, and choosing how to spend your limited resources is still important.

The new combat system is much more action-oriented, but it still retains some of the survival horror elements from the previous …

This game misses everything that makes a survival horror game fun. So it's good that it's not trying to be a survival horror game. This is a cheesy action game where you mindlessly mow down hoardes of Spaniards (good for those salty over the world cup this year). This game was revolutionary during its time and I can totally see why, it almost feels like the original DOOM in how basic of an outline it is for other games that copied its formula.

The game is played with an over-the-shoulder camera and lets you freely aim your gun using a lasersight, which I think is way more cool and unique than just a basic crosshair that's locked to the center of the screen. What I don't like about the lasersight however is that the dot disappears when you aim at something you can't shoot, which I find occansionally makes me lose track of where I'm aiming.

The game's greatest strength I think is the linear game design which means there's pretty much always something exciting happening as you play. There were however some sections of the game that I feel like should've had some branshing paths to let you choose what you want to do first and it can feel a little restrictive when you realize how "railroady" the game really is.

My biggest complaint with the game is definitely the final chapter, which is basically the final third of the whole thing. I think it very much overstays its welcome, since on my first playthrough it just made me feel numb to the whole game and on my Professional (hard mode) playthrough, it drove me absolutely mad. I also have some random frame drops here and there, nothing major, but still noticable and weird considering the game's age, hence why I've attached my PC Specs.

Only the second best 2005 Capcom game (I think we all know which one is the best)
8/10

citations.review_text:
Resident Evil 4 (2005) was my very first game in the Resident Evil series, and saying it impressed me would be a huge understatement. It completely hooked me and made me want to play the rest of the franchise.

The gameplay is incredibly well balanced. Sure, the controls feel a bit dated by today's standards(you can't move and shoot at the same time)but surprisingly, you get used to it very quickly because the entire game is designed around that limitation. Everything just works.

The developers absolutely nailed every aspect of the experience: memorable and varied locations, unforgettable boss fights, a satisfying weapon upgrade system, and a story that's definitely over-the-top but still incredibly fun and entertaining.

There's honestly not much more I can say that hasn't already been said. This game is a universally recognized masterpiece, and it's one of those rare cases where calling it "overrated" just doesn't make sense. Even though the Remake exists, I would never recommend skipping the original. It's still an amazing experience and absolutely worth playing.

10/10.

P.S. Unfortunately, I played through the game without the HD Project because I only found out about it after finishing the game. If you're playing on PC, I highly recommend installing it before your first playthrough. You can find a link to it in the Steam guides/workshop discussions, and it's absolutely worth it.

[h2]Nota Geral | Overall Rating[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]Resident Evil 4 original é um marco, não só da franquia, mas do gênero de ação como um todo, e joga-lo hoje em dia ainda mostra o motivo. A Capcom redefiniu o que um jogo de terror e ação poderia ser em 2005, e o impacto disso ainda é sentido em praticamente todo shooter em terceira pessoa lançado depois. Não é um jogo perfeito para os padrões atuais, a jogabilidade travada incomoda no começo, mas o pacote como um todo ainda segura muito bem o próprio peso.[/b]

[i]The original Resident Evil 4 is a landmark, not just for the franchise, but for the action genre as a whole, and playing it today still shows why. Capcom redefined what a horror and action game could be in 2005, and the impact of that is still felt in practically every third person shooter released since. It's not a perfect game by today's standards, the stiff controls are a bit uncomfortable at first, but the package as a whole still holds up remarkably well.[/i]

[h2]Jogabilidade | Gameplay[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]A jogabilidade é um tanto diferenciada, um pouco travada no início, cheguei a achar que não ia aguentar jogar. Você não anda e atira ao mesmo tempo, precisa parar para mirar, e isso, comparado com qualquer jogo moderno, soa como um defeito grave. Mas depois de uns 20 minutos eu acostumei, e foi aí que percebi que essa limitação é justamente o que dá tensão ao combate. Cada encontro vira uma decisão tática de posicionamento, já que você não pode simplesmente correr e atirar como faria em qualquer outro jogo de ação. O sistema de mira no corpo do inimigo, que gera reações diferentes dependendo de onde você acerta, ainda é genial mais de duas décadas depois.[/b]

citations.review_text:
A little bit of old jank but with all the action and cool mechanics, I can see why this is one of the GGOATs. Also, there is a ton of extra stuff once you finish your first playthrough.

Most of my deaths came from quick time events because the keys were kinda random.

Still holds up extremely well over 20 years later. Fun combat and brilliant pacing. Just wish that the QTEs had different button prompts as they can feel a bit awkward on keyboard and mouse. Mercenaries mode was also tons of fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that Ashley can be annoying due to her voice lines calling out for Leon and her AI occasionally taking poor paths or getting stuck during sections like the castle catapults.

citations.review_text:
The pinnacle of the Resident Evil series. A timeless masterpiece that changed the franchise by introducing the over the shoulder camera and shifting the focus toward action while reducing the emphasis on puzzles, which was a win for me.

That said, I almost dropped the game because of its awful controls. Once I switched to mouse and keyboard, though, the experience became much better. Despite being released in 2005, the game has aged remarkably well. It has everything a great game should have, along with an incredible amount of charm and personality.

For once, you're not confined to a single location. Instead, you explore an entire village, a massive castle, and an island, each introducing new enemies that speak Spanish and offering a unique atmosphere. Every boss fight feels different and memorable. Even though the game leans much more into action than horror, there were still several moments that genuinely creeped me out, whether because of the atmosphere or the occasional jump scare. I absolutely hated those traps.

The only part I felt neutral about was Ashley. Her voice became annoying after a while. "LEON!!!" is something I'll never forget. Her AI also shows its age. There were plenty of moments where she would take the worst possible path or simply stand still when I didn't tell her to. The castle was especially frustrating, particularly the catapult section, where she somehow managed to die almost every single time. As for technical issues, I only encountered two crashes while trying to reload a save, but nothing beyond that.

This game is a classic for a reason. It clearly takes inspiration from other games, like the radio communication style from Metal Gear, but it also introduced so many ideas of its own that it ended up influencing an entire generation of action games. If Resident Evil 4 were released today with modern graphics and a few quality of life improvements, I genuinely believe it would still be considered one of the best games on the market.

This game is a genuine masterpiece. Never properly played until now and it honestly holds up extremely well for a 21 year old game. The combat, gore, music, visuals, locations, enemies, characters, horror, story; all of it is really really good and was a joy to experience. However, a few sections were frustrating, main example being that god forsaken water room in Salazar's castle.... Additionally, Ashley herself can be annoying at times, especially with her incessant "HELP ME LEEOOON" any time she stubs her toe, although her AI and pathfinding are actually not bad at all for a 2005 game. All in all these issues aren't too bad. I did not hate the QTE stuff like most people do, I actually found some of it fun, especially Krauser's knife fight and dodging Verdugo's ceiling/floor attacks. Another thing I loved was the level design which reminded me alot of Dark Souls 1 especially in the beginning in the village areas. Best part of the game is the beloved merchant, my man. Wish he sold ammo though. Anyway I'm glad I finally played this. I will go on to play the remake to see how they compare, but I reckon this original version will be unbeatable.
